theme.title: Houston's high-volume years
theme.subtitle: Rockets, 2007–2019
theme.recap: Houston won 65 games, set a playoff record for missed threes and watched James Harden score 30 night after night.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2017–18 Rockets win?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: with their 59th win against the New Orleans Pelicans, eventually totalling 65 wins on the season

funFacts.text: The Rockets added Chris Paul from the Clippers that summer, pairing him with James Harden for a title push.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Rockets acquired star point guard Chris Paul from the Los Angeles Clippers

funFacts.text: Houston clinched the West's top seed for the first time in franchise history, finishing ahead of Golden State.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Rockets clinched the No. 1 seed for the first time in franchise history

funFacts.text: Before facing the Warriors, Houston eliminated Minnesota and Utah in five games apiece.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they defeated the Utah Jazz in five games

questions.prompt: In 2018–19, James Harden scored 30 or more in how many straight games?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: his 30-point streak which started on December 13, all the way to a surprising 32 games until ending on February 25.

funFacts.text: An early-season altercation between Chris Paul and Rajon Rondo became part of a turbulent Rockets campaign.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including an on-court altercation between rival guards Chris Paul and Rajon Rondo

funFacts.text: Trevor Ariza's departure and injuries contributed to Houston's rough start before Harden carried the recovery.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: injuries among its players, and losing core players including Trevor Ariza

funFacts.text: The Rockets recovered enough to claim another postseason berth, extending their playoff-appearance run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they clinched another playoff spot for the 7th straight year

questions.prompt: In Game 7 of the 2018 West finals, Houston set a playoff record by missing how many threes in a row?
questions.context: 2018 Western Conference finals · Game 7 · vs Golden State

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: set an NBA Playoff record by missing 27 straight 3-point shots

funFacts.text: Houston lost Chris Paul to a right hamstring injury late in Game 5; he missed the rest of the Warriors series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris Paul suffered a "right hamstring injury" in the final minute. He did not play for the rest of the series

funFacts.text: The Warriors entered the series as the West's second seed behind Houston, setting up a clash of the top two teams.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 2 | y – Golden State Warriors  *  | 58  | 24  | .707

funFacts.text: Golden State's win set up a fourth straight NBA Finals meeting with LeBron James's Cavaliers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first time the same two NBA teams met in the NBA Finals four seasons in a row

questions.prompt: Tracy McGrady stunned San Antonio in December 2004 by scoring how many points in the final 35 seconds?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: scoring 13 points in the final 35 seconds against the San Antonio Spurs

funFacts.text: Houston acquired McGrady from Orlando in a seven-player deal that also sent Steve Francis and Cuttino Mobley away.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: McGrady, Juwan Howard, Tyronn Lue, and Reece Gaines were traded to the Houston Rockets as part of a seven-player deal

funFacts.text: His late explosion included consecutive triples, one converted into a four-point play and another to win at the buzzer.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: one of which was part of a four-point play and the last of which was a game-winner in the final two seconds

funFacts.text: That Rockets team rebounded from a losing start and finished the season fifth in the West.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After the All-Star break, Houston rebounded from their slow start, finishing the season with 51 wins

questions.prompt: The 2007–08 Rockets won how many games in a row, then the second-longest streak ever?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Rockets went on a 22-game winning streak, which was the then-second longest in NBA history

funFacts.text: Yao Ming missed part of Houston's long streak, leaving a patchwork roster to keep winning without its star center.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: despite missing Yao Ming during that stretch

funFacts.text: Houston finished fifth in the West and drew a first-round rematch with the Utah Jazz.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Houston finished the season as the West's fifth seed, earning them a rematch with the Jazz in the first round

funFacts.text: McGrady scored forty in the decisive playoff Game 6, but Utah still eliminated Houston.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a strong 40-point and 10-rebound performance from McGrady in the decisive Game 6
